name: AI Engineer (@aiDotEngineer)
description: Official channel for AI Engineer events (World's Fair, Europe, Summit). Publishes all conference talks. The most comprehensive archive of AI engineering practitioner talks — 150+ talks from AIEWF 2025 alone. Primary source for finding new practitioners.

name: Latent Space
description: Video podcast companion to Latent Space (swyx + Alessio Fanelli). Technical deep dives with AI engineers and researchers. 10M+ readers/listeners across platforms.

name: Lenny's Podcast
description: Lenny Rachitsky's podcast covering product, growth, and increasingly AI tooling for builders. Filter for episodes about AI coding workflows, developer productivity, and product development with AI. Good signal for when AI tools cross into mainstream product-builder consciousness.

name: How I AI with Claire Vo
description: Practitioner AI workflow show on Lenny's Podcast network, hosted by Claire Vo. Live demos and workflow walkthroughs. Secondary signal after Lenny's main podcast — filter for episodes on AI coding or dev productivity.

name: Matt Pocock
description: Claude Code tutorials, TypeScript AI workflows, and skill authoring patterns. Creator of gstack-compatible skill sets, /grill-me, and Sandcastle. Highest-signal YouTube channel for Claude Code subscription + web app workflows.

name: Theo (t3.gg)
description: TypeScript/React + AI tooling commentary. Covers new AI dev tools from a pragmatic web app builder perspective. Good signal for what's gaining traction in the TS/React ecosystem.

name: Fireship
description: Rapid-fire 100-second and explainer-style coverage of new AI dev tools. Early signal for new tools gaining momentum. Good for tool discovery, less deep on implementation patterns.

name: Jack Herrington
description: TypeScript/React + AI integration tutorials. Hands-on demos of Claude Code and AI tooling with real web app projects. Good practical complement to Matt Pocock.

name: The Pragmatic Engineer
description: Gergely Orosz's channel covering AI's impact on software engineering. Interviews engineering leaders about AI transformation. Source of the widely-cited Jan-Feb 2026 AI tooling survey (~1000 respondents).
